name: Maletsunyane Falls
subtitle: Maletsunyane Falls, 192 metres high, lie at Semonkong, whose name means the place of smoke after the mist the falls throw up.

facts.label: Name of Semonkong
facts.value: The place of smoke, from the permanent smoke-like mist

facts.label: Geology
facts.value: Water plummets over a ledge of Triassic-Jurassic basalt

facts.label: Drought
facts.value: Reported by the Lesotho Times in January 2016 to have almost gone dry

facts.label: Abseil
facts.value: Semonkong Lodge runs an abseil described as the longest commercially operated single-drop abseil in the world

parts.text: Maletsunyane Falls, 192 metres high, lie at Semonkong, whose name means the place of smoke after the mist the falls throw up. The water drops over a ledge of Triassic-Jurassic basalt. In the 2015-16 drought the Lesotho Times reported that the falls had almost gone dry.
